cases.n: Black Axe in Palermo — 14 convicted (2018), 4 acquitted of mafia association (2019)
cases.who: Black Axe (Nigerian confraternity) cell in Palermo
cases.d: A Palermo police operation on 18 November 2016 arrested 19 alleged members of a Black Axe cell based in the Ballarò district; prosecutors said it ran debt collection, exploitation of prostitution and drug trafficking with mafia-style initiation rites. On 21 May 2018 a Palermo judge (fast-track procedure) convicted 14 Nigerians to a combined 87 years. In November 2019 the Palermo Corte d'Assise, trying five others, did not accept the mafia-association charge: four were acquitted and one was jailed for 11 years for kidnapping and sexual violence.
cases.cite: BlogSicilia, 21 May 2018; Il Fatto Quotidiano, 9 Nov 2019

cases.n: IOM: up to 80% of Nigerian women and girls arriving in Italy may be sex-trafficking victims
cases.victims_note: more than 11,000 Nigerian women and girls arrived by boat in 2016 (from 1,500 in 2014), at least four in five forced into prostitution, per IOM data cited by Thomson Reuters Foundation
cases.d: In July 2017 the International Organization for Migration said perhaps 80 per cent of Nigerian migrant women and girls arriving by sea in Italy could be sex-trafficking victims, and that its Italy office had seen an almost 600 per cent rise in potential victims over three years. IOM indicators included age (most victims 13–24) and being 'controlled' by other migrants. Thomson Reuters Foundation later cited IOM data that Nigerian female arrivals rose from 1,500 in 2014 to more than 11,000 in 2016.
cases.cite: UN News (IOM report), 21 Jul 2017; Thomson Reuters Foundation via The Peninsula, 19 Sep 2018

cases.n: Oba of Benin revokes trafficking 'juju' oaths (March 2018)
cases.who: Oba of Benin, Ewuare II; Edo traditional priests
cases.d: In March 2018 the Oba of Benin, Ewuare II, publicly revoked the curses that juju priests had used to bind trafficking victims to their traffickers and laid a curse on anyone involved in trafficking within his domain. Thomson Reuters Foundation reported in September 2018 that anecdotal evidence suggested trafficking had slowed, and cited UNODC that at least nine in ten Nigerian women trafficked to Europe come from Edo State.
cases.cite: New York Times, 24 Mar 2018 (via Wikipedia 'Ewuare II'); Thomson Reuters Foundation via The Peninsula, 19 Sep 2018

cases.n: Nigeria — cult-linked networks traffic women and girls to Europe and West African mines (US TIP 2025)
cases.who: Nigerian organized trafficking networks, some linked to cult organizations/confraternities
cases.d: The 2025 US Trafficking in Persons report says highly organized groups, sometimes linked to Nigerian cult organizations or confraternities, recruit and exploit Nigerian women and girls in sex trafficking in Italy, Spain and the UK, and that networks move women and girls to mining regions in Senegal, Mali, Burkina Faso and Côte d'Ivoire. In the reporting year courts convicted 49 traffickers and the government identified 2,058 victims. It describes corruption and official complicity, including among officials responsible for anti-trafficking, as significant concerns.
cases.cite: US Department of State, 2025 Trafficking in Persons Report — Nigeria

cases.n: Libya — sex trafficking of sub-Saharan girls in southern brothels; abuse of transiting children (US TIP 2025)
cases.who: Commercial sex rings; armed groups; officials
cases.cover: Observers report systemic official complicity, including Libyan Coast Guard, immigration and security officials; the government has never reported prosecuting or convicting anyone for sex or labour trafficking.
cases.d: The 2025 US TIP report says commercial sex rings subject sub-Saharan women and girls to sex trafficking in brothels, particularly in Ubari, Sabha and Murzuq, and that Nigerian women and girls are at increased risk. It cites an international organization finding that 77 per cent of children and youth transiting Libya experienced indicators of exploitation amounting to trafficking.
cases.cite: US Department of State, 2025 TIP Report — Libya

cases.n: Michael Pepe — former US Marine jailed 210 years for abusing girls in Cambodia
cases.victims_note: eight victims testified at the 2021 retrial; some were 9 years old
cases.who: Michael Joseph Pepe (retired US Marine Corps captain)
cases.d: Pepe travelled to Cambodia in 2005, was arrested there in 2006 and charged in the US in 2007. His first conviction was overturned by the Ninth Circuit in 2018; at a retrial in August 2021 victims testified he drugged, bound, beat and raped them, and prosecutors showed homemade abuse material. On 14 February 2022 a Los Angeles federal judge sentenced him to 210 years. The case was investigated by Homeland Security Investigations and the Cambodian National Police.
cases.cite: US Attorney's Office, Central District of California, 14 Feb 2022

cases.n: Ronald Boyajian — 70 years for buying a 9-year-old girl in Svay Pak
cases.victims_note: four victims aged 8–11 testified; conviction concerned a nine-year-old girl
cases.who: Ronald Gerard Boyajian (US registered sex offender)
cases.d: Boyajian, a registered sex offender with 1995 California convictions, was arrested in Cambodia in February 2009 on what prosecutors called his 35th trip to Asia over nine years, and was among the first three men expelled to the US under ICE's 'Operation Twisted Traveler' in August 2009. Convicted of illicit sexual conduct with a nine-year-old girl in Svay Pak, he was sentenced on 1 August 2016 to 70 years and ordered to pay $40,000 restitution.
cases.cite: US Attorney's Office, CDCA, 1 Aug 2016; AP via NBC News, 31 Aug 2009

cases.n: Operation Twisted Traveler — ICE crackdown on US offenders in Cambodia (2009)
cases.who: US Immigration and Customs Enforcement; Cambodian police
cases.d: In August 2009 three previously convicted US sex offenders arrested by Cambodian police in February — Ronald Boyajian, Erik Peeters and Jack Sporich — were returned to Los Angeles as the first defendants charged under 'Operation Twisted Traveler'. ICE head John Morton called Cambodia 'ground zero for child sex tourism'; ICE had stationed an agent in Cambodia full-time. Peeters was accused of abusing at least three Cambodian boys and Sporich of abusing a boy in Siem Reap (accusations at the time).
cases.cite: Associated Press via NBC News, 31 Aug 2009

cases.n: Svay Pak child brothels — 2003 raid and later decline
cases.cover: The 22 January 2003 police raid was widely advertised in advance; almost all children had been moved and no pimps or clients were arrested. Local authorities had extorted brothel owners.
cases.who: Brothels in Svay Pak (mostly ethnic Vietnamese victims)
cases.d: Brothels in Svay Pak, a village north of Phnom Penh, proliferated in the 1990s; in May 2000 there were 24 brothels with about 320 women on two streets, and in 2002 children, mostly ethnic Vietnamese sold by poor families, were exploited by Western child-sex tourists. A police raid in January 2003 after ministerial and ASEAN pressure was announced in advance. ABC News in 2017 found the share of children among those in sex work had fallen to 1–2% from 35%.
cases.cite: Wikipedia 'Svay Pak' (citing Haugen 2005, Daily Telegraph, Dateline NBC, ABC News 2017)

cases.n: Cambodia — child sex tourism and brothels; scam compounds (US TIP 2025)
cases.cover: The report says official complicity, including at senior levels, inhibited effective law enforcement.
cases.who: Brothel and entertainment operators; foreign and Cambodian offenders
cases.d: The 2025 US TIP report says Cambodian men and men from Australia, South Africa, the United States and other countries in Asia and Europe sexually exploit children in the tourism industry, increasingly via social media; children as young as 13 are exploited in brothels to pay family debts; and women and girls are exploited in online scam compounds.
cases.cite: US Department of State, 2025 TIP Report — Cambodia

nets.n: Black Axe (Neo-Black Movement of Africa confraternity)
nets.reach_note: US TIP 2025 says cult-linked Nigerian groups traffic women and girls in Italy, Spain, the UK and Germany but does not name Black Axe; only Italian prosecutions were verified here.
nets.d: Nigerian confraternity whose members in Italy were arrested in 2016 for 'mafia conspiracy, drug trafficking, exploitation of prostitution and violent crimes'. A Palermo court convicted 14 in 2018; in 2019 another Palermo court rejected the mafia-association charge for five others.
nets.cite: Wikipedia 'Black Axe (confraternity)'; BlogSicilia 2018; Il Fatto Quotidiano 2019

flows.n: Edo State → Libya → Italy (sex trafficking of women and girls)
flows.size_note: Nigerian female sea arrivals in Italy in 2016 (IOM data); at least four in five forced into prostitution
flows.d: Women and girls, most from Edo State, are moved overland through Niger and Libya and by boat to Italy, bound by debt and oaths. IOM recorded an almost 600 per cent rise in potential victims arriving by sea in 2014–2017.
flows.cite: IOM via UN News, Jul 2017; Thomson Reuters Foundation, Sep 2018

flows.n: Nigeria → gold-mining regions of Senegal, Mali, Burkina Faso, Côte d'Ivoire
flows.d: Organized networks transport Nigerian women and girls to mining regions in Senegal, Mali, Burkina Faso and Côte d'Ivoire for sex trafficking; in Kédougou victims include girls as young as 12.

flows.n: United States → Cambodia (travelling child sex offenders)
flows.size_note: three men returned under Operation Twisted Traveler in Aug 2009; Boyajian made 35 trips to Asia in nine years
flows.d: US men, several already convicted at home, travelled repeatedly to Cambodia to buy children; prosecuted in Los Angeles under the PROTECT Act.

flows.n: Vietnam → Svay Pak, Cambodia (girls sold to brothels)
flows.d: Most children in Svay Pak brothels were ethnic Vietnamese, many sold by destitute families; US TIP 2025 still reports ethnic Vietnamese women and girls exploited in Cambodian cities and tourist areas.
